newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares end mixed with no sign of upturn.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares end mixed with no sign of upturn.

text.p: Singapore shares ended mixed on Thursday with investors sidelined by concerns over the regional currency crisis and fears of a poor earnings season.
"There is not much to get investors excited about in this market at the moment," said one dealer at with a local firm.
"We've been caught in the crossfire of the regional currencies," added another.

At the close the Straits Times Industrials Index was fractionally higher, up 0.73 points to 1,967.14, in contrast to the Stock Exchange of Singapore property index which lost 2.3 percent or 15.66 points to 666.49.
"Virtually every company has property interests these days and if that's down the whole market feels it," one dealer said.
City Developments dropped Singapore $0.40 to S$12.50 while Keppel Land shed 4.6 percent of its value or S$0.20 to S$4.20.

Asia Food & Properties continued to pay the price for its rescue of Amcol Holdings, closing at a new low for the year of US$0.89, down US$0.09 on the day. The shares are now US$0.55 off their July 18 debut high.
Top loser though was DBS Bank foreign stock, down S$0.60 at S$19.10.
Singapore Press foreign stock was the day's biggest gainer, up S$1.10 to S$27.90.
